verdict.rationale: AgentMail's own hosted MCP server is documented as exposing "calendar tools" alongside inbox and message tools, so some first-party calendar capability exists. The evidence never says what those tools do, and AgentMail is an API-first agent inbox rather than a human-facing email client with calendar UI. Older snapshots of the same MCP page (docs-12, docs-23) list no calendar tools, which suggests the feature is new or thinly documented. Missing for 10: documented calendar viewing, invite accept/decline handling, event creation, an in-client (non-API) calendar experience, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can see my calendar, respond to invites, and create events without leaving the email client

citations.quote: exposes inbox, message, thread, draft, attachment, and calendar tools to any compatible client
AgentMail runs a hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.agentmail.to/mcp` that exposes inbox, message, thread, draft, attachment, and calendar tools
